description:
## Problem
Seventeen pages under benchbox-site `docs/reference/python-api/benchmarks/` describe the constructor's `scale_factor` as 'Must be positive'. Constructing a benchmark class directly does accept any positive value for most benchmarks, but every supported run path (command line, runner, MCP) applies the range rule from BenchBox#4126: 0.01 to 100000, whole numbers from 1, and a fixed value for `joinorder` and `metadata_primitives`. The pages do not say that a value the constructor accepts can still be refused when the benchmark is run.

This is site-only work. It is filed here because the session that found it was bound to the core tracker; move it to the benchbox-site tracker if preferred.

## Change
On each page, state the constructor's own check accurately and add one sentence, or a link to the Scale factors section of `docs/benchmarks/index.md`, giving the range that applies when the benchmark is run. For TPC-DS and TPC-DS-OBT the constructor itself enforces 0.01; those two pages are already correct.

## Guardrails
- Verify each page's statement against the class constructor on current core `develop`; do not copy one sentence to all pages unchecked.
- The Python API headings are contract-checked; keep headings unchanged.
